mentions.story: Ask HN: Free or cheap UI design course?
mentions.text:
Very good course (teaches UX from fundamentals): [course]

Currently it costs $75, but Udemy often has coupons/promotions for up to 95% off (I registered for $15). This course is normally $5000+. It is very thorough and well-explained. Like 20+ hours of video lectures, slides and full transcripts. Also the instructor is very responsive and active in the course's private FB group.

This course is shorter and more focused on web UI (vs more general UX): [link]

You can probably find resources for free, but then you might end up paying with your time. If you're really strapped for cash, I suggest borrowing books from the library: free and probably better than a lot of the low-cost/free…

mentions.text:
Here's a list of books I've put together for classes:
[link]

MIT's OCW class on UI - [course]

Also, look at RISD, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Cornell (in no particular order).

If you can, anything by Doug Engelbart is amazingly motivational (inventor of the mouse) and insightful.

If you contact me, I'd be happy to send you my slides from lectures I've done on interaction and answer any questions.

mentions.author: SingAlong
mentions.story: Ask YC: Have you come across any good interface for a search engine?
mentions.text:
Google recognises only document formats and shows them.

I meant recognising what the page actually contains? Is the page a simple HTML page or a very heavy flash page. This would help people in low bandwidth countries like Africa.

And it would be a lot better if you have a basic idea of what you want to display and create an image mockup, post it here and ask for feedback (after you get enough ideas from this thread). That would be the next thing you would want to do I suppose. That way you would be able to get more inputs for a close-to-perfect redesign. :)

Also,
[course]

Thats the link to the MIT User Interface Design course from MIT OCW. Refer that for a better UI.
